rubric.task_read: This is an enormous, long-horizon software build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent server, JSON API, ~150-function formula engine with dynamic-array spilling, LET/LAMBDA, Excel error propagation, dirty-only recompute under hard perf budgets, copy/fill/sort/filter, CSV + openpyxl-compatible XLSX round-trip, a vanilla SPA with fixed testids, a WebSocket collab protocol with op/seq/presence semantics, and an 'analyst surface' of names/formats/conditional-formatting/pivots/locale/validation, plus iterative calc and Goal Seek). The wire contract is not specified in prose — it is defined by an existing client at /dev_tests/helpers.py — and grading is against a hidden suite far larger than the provided smoke tests, benchmarked cell-by-cell against LibreOffice ground truth. Difficulty comes from (a) reverse-engineering an implicit contract, (b) breadth (dozens of loosely-coupled subsystems) far exceeding what can be perfected, and (c) semantic correctness against a precise external oracle (Excel/LibreOffice). A skilled practitioner would therefore invest heavily and continuously in orientation, decomposition/sequencing, self-built verification against Excel semantics, and breadth-vs-depth triage — this is near the top of the range for every meta-work faculty.

dimensions.name: Contract reverse-engineering & semantic grounding
dimensions.description: Reading /dev_tests/helpers.py and run.sh to recover the exact wire shapes, and grounding formula/error/spill behavior in precise Excel-365 semantics before and during implementation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The entire wire contract (workbook ids, cell shapes, patch/fill/sort bodies, kind discriminator, spill fields, listing envelope) is defined only by the existing client — guessing it means every endpoint fails the hidden suite. Correctness is graded against LibreOffice, so function/error/spill semantics must be understood, not improvised.

anchors.0: Starts implementing endpoints and formulas from the prose alone; never opens helpers.py; invents its own JSON shapes.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once, copies a couple of obvious shapes, but leaves most contract details (spill fields, error names, envelope keys) to guesswork; treats Excel semantics as 'roughly known'.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh, extracts the concrete request/response shapes it will implement first, and confirms a few endpoints against the smoke suite; consults Excel behavior for the common functions.
anchors.8: Systematically maps helpers.py into a working model of every wire shape it touches, cross-checks against run.sh, and proactively probes ambiguous semantics (spill materialization, error precedence, criteria/wildcard rules, locale separators) against known Excel behavior before coding them.
anchors.10: Sustains contract/semantic research across the whole build: builds and updates a precise internal spec of shapes and edge-cases from the client, re-derives behavior from the oracle whenever a subsystem is entered (e.g. XLSX numFmt/definedName layout, collab seq ordering, iterative-calc fixpoint), and catches subtle contract details a casual reading would miss — never coding a subsystem blind.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & thin-slice sequencing
dimensions.description: Breaking the vast surface into an ordered hierarchy — enabling skeleton (bootable server + health + persistence) first, then core cell/recompute model, then formula engine, then the many independent advanced features — each with a concrete done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Dozens of loosely-coupled subsystems with dependencies (recompute underlies formulas underlies spill underlies collab/xlsx). Without deliberate sequencing and an end-to-end slice early, the agent risks a large pile of half-wired parts that never boots or verifies.

anchors.0: No visible structure; jumps between unrelated features (a pivot here, a distribution function there) with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat to-do list of feature names with no dependency ordering and no explicit 'done' definition per item.
anchors.5: Identifies major components and works in a sensible order (skeleton/health → cell model → engine → advanced), with rough milestones tied to running the smoke tests.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone plan that gets a thin end-to-end slice (server boots, health OK, basic cell patch + one formula + persistence survives restart) working early, then layers subsystems each with a stated done-check, so the system is continuously runnable.
anchors.10: Maintains a living, dependency-ordered milestone hierarchy that keeps a working spine at all times, decomposes hard subsystems (spill engine, XLSX round-trip, collab protocol) into independently verifiable sub-milestones with crisp exit criteria, and re-sequences as dependencies and discoveries dictate — never leaving the system in an unbootable half-integrated state.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification against the Excel oracle
dimensions.description: Deliberately designing checks beyond the non-exhaustive smoke suite — running the server and exercising endpoints, comparing formula/error results to Excel semantics, verifying perf budgets, XLSX re-import via openpyxl, and collab flows.
dimensions.why_it_matters: run.sh is explicitly non-exhaustive and grading is a much larger hidden suite scored cell-by-cell against LibreOffice. Assuming success because smoke tests pass would leave most behavior unverified; the agent must construct its own evidence of correctness.

anchors.0: Never runs the server or tests; assumes code works because it was written.
anchors.3: Runs run.sh occasionally and eyeballs output; no checks for functions/edge-cases/perf/xlsx beyond what the smoke suite happens to cover.
anchors.5: Runs the server and the smoke suite, manually exercises a few endpoints, and spot-checks some formula results against expected Excel values.
anchors.8: Builds targeted checks beyond the smoke suite: verifies representative functions per category against known Excel outputs, exercises error propagation and spill/#SPILL! cases, checks a perf scenario against the stated budgets, and round-trips an XLSX through openpyxl to confirm formulas/values/names/formats survive.
anchors.10: Establishes a systematic, oracle-grounded verification regime: reusable harnesses that check many functions and edge-cases against Excel/LibreOffice-equivalent expectations, explicit tests for the hard invariants (topological dirty-only recompute correctness, iterative-calc convergence values, collab seq ordering / LWW, ValidationError/SpillTargetWriteError paths, restart persistence), and perf measurements against each budget — treating a passing smoke suite as necessary-but-insufficient throughout.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across a huge feature surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate done-vs-remaining picture across the many subsystems and function families, and detecting when stuck on a hard corner (parser, spill, xlsx) rather than silently dropping scope.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The feature list is so large that it is easy to lose track of what is implemented, believe coverage is higher than it is, or sink unbounded time into one stubborn subsystem while dozens of others remain untouched.

anchors.0: No sense of overall coverage; forgets whole subsystems; repeats or abandons work without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; realizes late that major areas (e.g. locale, pivots, collab) were never addressed; no awareness of time sunk on a stuck item.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of subsystems/functions and updates it as items complete, with a rough sense of what remains.
anchors.8: Maintains an accurate, regularly-updated coverage map of subsystems and function families, notices when a subsystem is churning without progress, and consciously time-boxes or defers it to protect overall coverage.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise, continuously-reconciled picture of implemented/verified/remaining across the entire surface, distinguishes 'written' from 'verified', catches thrashing early (e.g. re-debugging the same spill or parser issue in circles) and names it, and keeps the horizon in view so no major area is silently lost.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified contract/design assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising wire-shape assumptions, engine design, or library choices when the client, the oracle, or perf/round-trip reality contradicts them — rather than pressing on with a broken premise.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Because the contract is inferred and correctness/perf are externally judged, early assumptions (a shape, a recompute design, an OOXML or formula library) will be falsified. Detecting and reworking these quickly is decisive; barrelling ahead propagates one wrong assumption across dozens of endpoints.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps building on a shape or design the client/tests have already shown to be wrong.
anchors.3: Patches individual symptoms without revisiting the underlying wrong assumption; repeats the same failure elsewhere.
anchors.5: When a test or run contradicts an assumption, fixes it and applies the correction to the obviously affected places.
anchors.8: Treats contradictions as signals about the model: traces a failure back to the wrong assumption (shape, semantics, or design), revises it centrally, and re-checks other subsystems that shared it.
anchors.10: Runs a tight expectation-vs-reality loop throughout: proactively surfaces where the inferred contract or a design choice (recompute strategy, spill model, xlsx/formula library, iterative solver) is failing, makes decisive architectural corrections rather than accreting patches, and re-verifies dependent subsystems after each pivot — never sustaining progress on a premise it has already seen falsified.

dimensions.name: Breadth-vs-depth triage for hidden-suite coverage
dimensions.description: Deliberately allocating limited effort across an infeasibly large feature surface to maximize verified coverage — prioritizing high-yield, broadly-tested behavior over perfecting one niche corner.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec lists far more than can be implemented flawlessly, and grading rewards broad cell-by-cell correctness. The distinctive meta-move here is triage: choosing which functions/subsystems to build and harden first for maximum expected score, and consciously deferring low-yield exotica — a demand distinct from mere ordering (decomposition) because it trades depth against breadth under a fixed budget.

anchors.0: Sinks disproportionate effort into a single niche corner (e.g. one distribution function or engineering conversions) while core, heavily-tested paths remain broken or absent.
anchors.3: Implements features in arbitrary order with no regard to expected test yield; over-polishes rare cases and under-serves common ones.
anchors.5: Roughly prioritizes common, high-value behavior (core math/lookup/text, basic recompute, persistence) before exotic features, with some awareness of the breadth budget.
anchors.8: Makes explicit, defensible triage calls — securing the broadest, most-likely-tested behavior across categories first, hardening it to verified quality, and consciously deferring or stubbing low-yield exotica — to maximize coverage under limited effort.
anchors.10: Runs continuous expected-value triage across the whole build: reasons about which subsystems and function families the hidden suite most likely weights, deliberately breadth-first to a verified baseline before selective deepening, and re-allocates as coverage and time evidence accrue — extracting maximal graded coverage from an infeasible surface rather than exhausting the budget on a favorite subsystem.
